title: Add default OG / Twitter card image across all pages
problem: Every page is missing og:image and twitter:card image. When shared on social platforms (X/Twitter, LinkedIn, Slack), no preview image is shown; Twitter falls back to a text-only summary card with no visual, directly reducing click-through on social shares.
proposal: Create a single 1200×630 px fallback OG image (public/og-default.png) and add og:image / twitter:image meta tags to BaseLayout.astro. Accept an optional image prop (defaulting to the fallback) so SectionEntryLayout can generate page-specific images in future. Upgrade twitter:card from summary to summary_large_image once an image is present.
evidence: dist/index.html: no og:image or twitter:image tag in <head>. dist/concepts/what-is-an-agent/index.html: same. public/ directory contains only ads.txt and robots.txt — no image assets of any kind. src/layouts/BaseLayout.astro line 34: <meta name='twitter:card' content='summary'> with no image tag following.
open_questions: Should per-page OG images be generated at build time (e.g. via @vercel/og or satori), or is a single static fallback sufficient for now?
What branding elements should appear on the OG image (title, site name, accent color)?
mockup_hint: code diff — before/after showing added og:image and twitter:image meta tags in BaseLayout.astro, plus upgrade twitter:card to summary_large_image

title: Code-block copy button with language badge
problem: Several Deep-Dive and Concept entries contain <pre> code blocks. None of these blocks have a copy-to-clipboard button or a visible language label badge. Readers who want to run or adapt code snippets must manually select all text, which is error-prone on mobile. No browser renders a native copy affordance on pre-formatted blocks.
proposal: Inject a copy button and optional language badge into every <pre> block client-side via a small vanilla JS snippet (~30 lines) added to BaseLayout.astro (or the two detail layouts). The script querySelectorAll('pre') after DOMContentLoaded, inserts a <button class='copy-btn'> absolutely positioned top-right of each pre, and wires navigator.clipboard.writeText. Button label is bilingual via data-copy/data-copied attributes reading document.documentElement.lang. A language badge (e.g. 'python', 'json') appears top-left if data-lang is set. Pure static, no framework dependency.
evidence: The Prompt Engineering Guide shows copy buttons on every prompt/code block with a visible language indicator. This feature was observed across nearly every peer site that contains code — it is now a baseline reader expectation for technical documentation, not a differentiator. MDN, GitHub, and Astro docs all ship this. The site already loads inline scripts (SiteSearch, tab-switcher) so the pattern is established.
open_questions: Should the button only appear on <pre class='standalone'> or on all <pre>? Scoping to .standalone avoids false positives.
Does the copy button need a bilingual 'Copy'/'复制' label, or is a clipboard icon SVG sufficient to avoid i18n complexity?
Content fragments are raw HTML rendered via set:html — authors need a convention for marking language (e.g. <pre data-lang='python'>). Should we default to 'code' when no data-lang is present?
mockup_hint: Each <pre> block gains position:relative. In the top-right corner a small button (24x24px, rounded 4px, background: var(--paper-2), border: 1px solid var(--ink) at 20% opacity) displays a clipboard icon SVG. On hover the border darkens. On click it switches to a checkmark for 1.5s then reverts. In top-left a <span class='lang-badge'> in 9px JetBrains Mono uppercase shows the language name if data-lang is set.

title: RSS / Atom feed for the Changelog
problem: The Changelog page already tracks dated content additions and changes, which is exactly the data an RSS feed should expose. However, there is no RSS or Atom feed anywhere on the site — no <link rel='alternate'> in the <head>, no feed URL in the footer. Readers who follow many technical resources via feed readers have no way to subscribe to wiki updates, breaking the return loop for power users entirely.
proposal: Generate a static /rss.xml at build time using Astro's @astrojs/rss package (zero new dependencies in the Astro 4 ecosystem). Iterate CHANGELOG entries (already a flat sorted array) and emit one <item> per entry. A matching /zh/rss.xml emits the same dates with title[zh] and items[zh] bullets. Add <link rel='alternate' type='application/rss+xml'> in BaseLayout.astro <head> and a small RSS icon link in SiteFooter.astro.
evidence: Simon Willison prominently links an Atom feed at the top of every page and reports it as a primary distribution channel. Eugene Yan credits RSS for a significant fraction of recurring readers. MDN, the Rust blog, and Astro's own docs all ship RSS. The /zh/ URL prefix pattern is already established for bilingual routes. The Changelog data structure is already a flat sorted array ready to iterate.
open_questions: Should each changelog item be a separate feed item, or one item per changelog entry (date + title + bullets)? One item per entry is simpler.
Should Deep-Dive and Concept new-entry additions also generate feed items, or only changelog-level entries?
Vercel caches static assets aggressively — does the feed need a Cache-Control header override in vercel.json to expire promptly after each deploy?
mockup_hint: SiteFooter gains a second line below the copyright: 'RSS · EN | RSS · 中文' in JetBrains Mono 10px, with each term linking to /rss.xml and /zh/rss.xml. BaseLayout.astro adds a <link rel='alternate' type='application/atom+xml' title='Agentic AI Wiki Changelog' href='/rss.xml'> in the <head>.

title: Deep-Dives index group jump-nav
problem: The Deep-Dives index is a single scrollable page with 75+ entries across 12 groups and no anchor jump-nav at the top. A reader who wants 'Safety & Security' must scroll past 30+ entries (Architectures, Protocols, Memory, RAG) to reach it. The section will only grow, compounding the problem.
proposal: Add a sticky-within-page group anchor bar at the top of the Deep-Dives index (below the hero): one pill/badge per group linking to its anchor. The group headers in SectionIndexView already render as .toc-part-label divs — add id attributes keyed by group slug and render the anchor bar from the same groups array. No manifest schema change needed.
evidence: SectionIndexView.astro renders groups.map(g => <div class='toc-part'>...) with no id attributes. NAVIGATION-PLAN.md §2 P4 flagged this at 51 entries; the worktree now has 75 entries across 12 groups (counted from src/content/deep-dives/groups/*.ts). The live page at https://agentic-ai-wiki.vercel.app/deep-dives confirms no jump-nav exists.
open_questions: Should the same jump-nav appear on the Concepts index (only 4 groups — lower urgency but nice consistency)?
Sticky within-page vs static — does sticky conflict with the sticky site-header at 56px?
mockup_hint: Draw the Deep-Dives index page. Below the hero lede, before the first group, show a horizontally-scrolling strip of small uppercase badges (JetBrains Mono, 10px) — one per group. Each badge is a link; clicking scrolls to that group header. On mobile the strip is horizontally scrollable. The currently-visible group badge gets the accent underline as the reader scrolls.

title: Mobile prev/next nav on section detail pages
problem: On screens ≤900px the .chapter-side sidebar is hidden entirely and replaced with a single 'Browse all X →' back-link. This means mobile readers have no way to navigate to the adjacent entry — no prev/next, no sibling context. The prev/next buttons that exist at the bottom of every detail page are the only escape route, and they are invisible until the reader reaches the very end of a long article.
proposal: Add a compact prev/next strip immediately after the .mobile-section-nav back-link (which already exists and is shown only on mobile). The strip uses the same prev/next data already computed in SectionEntryLayout.astro (prev and next variables). It requires no new data: just two short <a> tags with ← / → arrows and the sibling title, styled to fit in a single line at small viewport.
evidence: site.css line 86-90: @media (max-width: 900px) { .chapter-side { display:none; } .mobile-section-nav { display: block; } }. SectionEntryLayout.astro lines 34-36 already compute prev and next. The bottom .page-nav already renders them — it's just too far away on mobile after a long article.
competitor_examples: MDN Web Docs mobile prev/next at article top
open_questions: Should the same top prev/next strip be added to the Field Guide's ChapterLayout as well?
Title truncation: deep-dive titles can be long — use ellipsis or shorten to just the first clause?
mockup_hint: Draw a mobile viewport (375px wide) of a Concepts or Deep-Dives detail page. Just below the 'Browse all Concepts →' back-link, show a two-column row: left cell has '← prev' in muted mono caps and the previous entry's title in Fraunces serif (truncated with ellipsis if needed); right cell has 'next →' and the next title, right-aligned. Separated from the back-link by a thin rule.

title: Add a 'Multi-Agent Systems' Concept entry
problem: The Concepts encyclopedia has no entry for multi-agent systems, yet the Deep-Dives section dedicates a full six-essay group to it and the Field Guide dedicates chapter x4. A reader on the Concepts index who wants to understand what multi-agent systems are has no on-ramp — they must jump directly into advanced essays or a full Field Guide chapter without foundational framing.
proposal: Add a new Concept entry with slug multi-agent-systems, group Agentic AI, positioned after when-to-use-an-agent. Cover: why one agent is the default, what properties justify splitting (parallelism, specialization, context isolation), the coordination tax, and a clear pointer to the Deep-Dive group and Field Guide chapter x4. Requires bilingual HTML pair and a manifest.ts insertion.
evidence: src/content/concepts/manifest.ts (no multi-agent entry in Agentic AI group); src/content/deep-dives/groups/multi-agent-systems.ts (6-entry group); src/content/field-guide/manifest.ts (chapter x4 = multi-agent); src/content/field-guide/en/x4.html (extensive treatment with no foundational concept to point back to).
open_questions: Should it be placed before or after when-to-use-an-agent to preserve the logical progression from single-agent to multi-agent?
Should the group label remain Agentic AI or be a new Agentic AI (Advanced) sub-group?
mockup_hint: Four-step structure mirroring existing Agentic AI concepts. Step 1: the default position (one agent with tools). Step 2: the three honest justifications for splitting (parallelism, specialization, fault isolation). Step 3: the coordination tax — why multi-agent is not free. Step 4: a decision one-liner plus xref callout pointing to the Deep-Dives group and Field Guide chapter x4. One ASCII diagram showing a supervisor dispatching to two workers.

title: Persistent reading progress via localStorage
problem: The Field Guide is a 22-chapter linear course with no indication of how far a reader has progressed. Returning readers must remember or scroll the sidebar to find where they left off. The home page always shows 'Start reading →' with no personalisation — it cannot distinguish a first-time visitor from someone 18 chapters in.
proposal: On each Field Guide chapter page, write localStorage.setItem('fg-last', slug) on DOMContentLoaded (inline script, no library). On the home page and field-guide index, read fg-last and if set, replace 'Start reading →' with 'Continue: <chapter title> →'. In ChapterSidebar, mark already-visited slugs (stored as a JSON array in fg-visited) with a subtle filled dot. All logic is ~25 lines of vanilla JS. Bilingual: locale-aware keys (fg-last-en / fg-last-zh) and chapter titles from existing page data attributes.
evidence: Linear courses (web.dev Learn, javascript.info, learnpython.org) universally track progress because it is the single biggest drop-off point — people forget where they left off and give up. The Field Guide is structured exactly like a course: 6 parts, 22 ordered chapters. No backend, no auth: localStorage is exactly the right primitive.
open_questions: Should 'Continue reading' replace or supplement 'Start reading →' on the home page? Supplementing (showing both) is safer.
How should visited state be represented in the sidebar — a dot, a checkmark, a strikethrough? A small filled dot is least invasive.
Should progress reset on the ZH locale independently from EN, or share state? Separate keys make locale switching clean.
mockup_hint: Draw two states of the home page featured card side by side. Left: first-time visitor — 'Start reading →'. Right: returning visitor who left off at chapter 12 — 'Continue: Observability & Tracing →' with a small progress indicator '12 / 22 chapters'. Draw the ChapterSidebar with the first 11 chapters showing a small filled circle (visited) and chapter 12 highlighted as current.

title: In-page scroll-spy table of contents for long entries
problem: Deep-Dive essays and Concept entries already have rich internal heading structure, but there is no in-page TOC that tracks the reader's scroll position. On entries with 6+ h2/h3 headings the reader loses context of where they are in the document. Peer documentation sites treat this as a baseline feature for content this long.
proposal: Add a right-rail 'On This Page' TOC component that extracts h2/h3 headings from the rendered article at build time or via client-side querySelectorAll on DOMContentLoaded. Highlight the active section via IntersectionObserver — no backend required, pure CSS/JS. Render bilingual label ('On this page' / '本页目录'). On mobile (<900px), convert to a collapsible accordion at the top of the article.
evidence: The Prompt Engineering Guide shows an 'On This Page' right-rail sidebar that lists h2 anchors and highlights the current section as the reader scrolls. Chip Huyen's blog renders a detailed TOC at the start of long posts. Both patterns dramatically reduce the need to scroll back to orient oneself in a long technical article.
open_questions: Content is injected via set:html — heading extraction must happen client-side (querySelectorAll) or via an Astro build-time remark/rehype plugin.
Right rail requires a third column in the chapter-shell grid — does this break the existing 1180px max-width budget on mid-size screens?
Should the TOC be hidden when an entry has fewer than 3 headings to avoid showing a near-empty rail?
mockup_hint: A fixed-width (180px) 'On This Page' panel sits to the right of the article prose column. Label in JetBrains Mono uppercase 10px. Each h2 heading is a clickable link; the currently-visible section gets a 2px left border in the accent colour. Below 900px the panel is hidden and replaced by a collapsed <details> accordion at the top of the article.

title: Scope Deep-Dives sidebar to current group
problem: The sidebar on a Deep-Dives detail page renders all 75 entries across all 12 groups — an extremely long, dense list that overwhelms the sidebar's navigational value. The active entry is buried somewhere in the middle. The reader cannot tell at a glance which group they are in or how many peers it has.
proposal: Pass only the current group's entries to SectionSidebar, plus a compact group switcher above the list: a small static list of all group names where the current group is expanded and highlighted. A small '↑ All groups' link at the bottom of the sidebar returns to the Deep-Dives index. Keeps the sidebar scannable (6-9 entries instead of 75) while preserving cross-group navigation.
evidence: DeepDiveLayout.astro passes all 75 entries, 12 groups to SectionSidebar. At 75 entries the sidebar is already impractical; NAVIGATION-PLAN.md §1 pain point #6 and §2 P4 flag this. The react-pattern detail page live fetch confirmed the sidebar lists all groups and many entries.
open_questions: Should Concepts sidebar also be scoped (4 groups, 33 entries — less urgent but consistent)?
For the group switcher: static list (simpler, no JS, accessible) or CSS-only accordion? Static is lower risk.
Does scoping the sidebar break the bilingual parity requirement? (No — group names are already localised in the manifest.)
mockup_hint: Draw two sidebar states side by side. Left (current): a very long list of all 12 group headings with many entries, active entry barely visible. Right (proposed): a short group switcher at the top showing all 12 group names as small mono uppercase links, with 'Architectures & Patterns' highlighted. Below it, an expanded list of only the 8 entries in that group, the active one accented. At the bottom a small '← All Deep-Dives' link.

title: End-of-article 'Graduate to' CTA block
problem: Every concept and deep-dive article ends with prev/next within-section navigation — good for sequential readers but insufficient for the reader who just finished 'What is RAG?' and wants to know what to read next in a different section. The cross-section relationship (Concept → Deep-Dive → Field Guide chapter) is unmapped at the page level.
proposal: Add an optional graduate field (array of { section: 'field-guide'|'concepts'|'deep-dives', slug: string }) to the manifest Entry type for Concepts and Deep-Dives. At the bottom of SectionEntryLayout, if entry.graduate is non-empty, render a small card row titled 'Go deeper →' (EN) / '深入了解 →' (ZH) linking to those entries. Fall back gracefully if graduate is absent. Graduate links resolve at build time using existing ENTRIES + CHAPTERS lookups, so dead links are build errors.
evidence: NAVIGATION-PLAN.md explicitly calls this out as P2 ('Related pages') and P3 ('prev/next + graduate to'). High-value pairs already identified: RAG → Advanced RAG Architectures; Agent Loop → ReAct; Tool Calling → Tool-Calling Standards; Agentic Risks → Agentic Threat Model. This is a scoped, lower-effort version of P2 using a separate graduate field rather than the heavier related: slug[] mechanism.
open_questions: Should graduate be added to the manifest Entry type (schema change, touches verify script) or delivered as a separate static map file?
Should graduate links be one-directional (Concepts → Deep-Dives, Concepts → Field Guide) or bidirectional? Starting one-directional is simpler.
How many graduate links are too many? Suggest capping at 3 to keep the card compact.
mockup_hint: Draw the bottom of a concept detail page (e.g. 'What is RAG?') below the article text and above the prev/next nav. Show a lightly bordered card row titled 'Go deeper →' with two entry cards side by side: one for a Deep-Dive ('Advanced RAG Architectures') and one for a Field Guide chapter ('Retrieval'). Each card has a small section kicker label in the accent color above the entry title.

title: Dark mode toggle with system-preference default
problem: The site uses a fixed light theme with no dark mode toggle and no prefers-color-scheme media query in the CSS. In 2026 the majority of developer audiences prefer dark mode, especially when reading long technical content. Every direct peer site observed either has dark mode or is actively building it.
proposal: Add a dark-mode CSS layer using @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) overrides for the existing :root colour tokens in guide.css, plus an optional manual toggle (sun/moon SVG button in SiteHeader.astro) that writes 'theme' to localStorage and applies a data-theme='dark' attribute to <html>. The script is ~20 lines of vanilla JS inlined in BaseLayout.astro before the body to prevent FOUC.
evidence: The Prompt Engineering Guide has a prominent 'Light/Dark' toggle in the top navigation. Anthropic's own research pages reference dark mode in their footer links. The Hugging Face agents course defaults to dark mode. This was the single most consistent gap observed across all peer benchmarks.
open_questions: How many distinct colour tokens need dark variants? The palette uses --paper, --paper-2, --ink, --muted, --accent, --accent-ink — all need inverting.
Do embedded AdSense units render acceptably in dark mode, or do they flash light backgrounds?
Should the toggle state persist across locale switches (en ↔ zh), and how does this interact with SSR vs. client-side localStorage?
mockup_hint: A 28x28px circular icon button (sun in light mode, moon in dark mode) sits at the far right of the SiteHeader, just before the lang-switch nav. Clicking toggles data-theme='dark' on <html> and saves to localStorage. Dark palette: --paper becomes #0f0f0f, --paper-2 #1a1a1a, --ink #e8e4dc, --muted #7a7672, --accent unchanged.

title: Add Pagefind section filters to scope search by content type
problem: The search index is a flat, undifferentiated corpus with no way for users to filter results to a specific section (Field Guide vs. Concepts vs. Deep-Dives). All data-pagefind-filter and data-pagefind-meta attributes are absent from the built HTML. A query like 'tool use' returns a noisy mix of entries from all three content types with no way to narrow results.
proposal: Add data-pagefind-filter='section:<SectionName>' to the <main> element in each detail layout: section:Field Guide in ChapterLayout.astro, section:Concepts in SectionEntryLayout, and section:Deep Dives in DeepDiveLayout.astro. Then pass filters: true to the PagefindUI constructor in SiteSearch.astro so the filter UI is rendered.
evidence: src/components/SiteSearch.astro lines 95–102: PagefindUI constructor has no filters key. grep -r 'data-pagefind-filter' src/ returns no results. The search corpus includes all 135 en content pages (field-guide, concepts, deep-dives) indexed together with no differentiation.
open_questions: Should the filter UI display section labels in both English and Chinese depending on locale?
Does Pagefind's language-scoped indexing (per html lang) interact with section filters — i.e. do EN and ZH pages need separate filter values?
mockup_hint: code diff — SectionEntryLayout.astro adding data-pagefind-filter to article element; SiteSearch.astro adding filters option to PagefindUI constructor showing a filter panel with checkboxes for Field Guide, Concepts, Deep Dives

title: Reading-path callout on Concepts and Deep-Dives index pages
problem: A newcomer landing on /concepts or /deep-dives sees a flat list of grouped entries with no recommended entry point, no sense of which entries to read first, and no pointer to the Field Guide as the structured path. The Concepts tagline promises orientation but the page delivers none.
proposal: Add a small 'New here?' callout block between the hero and the entry list in SectionIndexView. For Concepts: suggest a five-entry core path (what-is-an-llm → what-is-an-agent → the-agent-loop → tool-calling-explained → what-is-rag) as a horizontal chip list with a 'or follow the guided Field Guide →' escape. For Deep-Dives: a one-liner 'These essays assume Concepts fluency — new? Start with Concepts →'. All copy lives in src/i18n/ui.ts (bilingual).
evidence: NAVIGATION-PLAN.md §2 P1 (unshipped). HomeView.astro already links Concepts with its tagline but never names an entry point. The five-entry core path is already named in NAVIGATION-PLAN.md §2 P1.
open_questions: Should the five-entry Concepts path be rendered as a mini horizontal chip-list or as a simple prose sentence?
Does the zh translation need a different core-path sentence or is it a straight translation of the en text?
mockup_hint: Draw the Concepts index page. Between the page hero and the first group ('AI Foundations'), insert a bordered callout box (using the existing .callout.tip CSS style — green 'TIP' badge). Inside: 'New to agentic AI? Read these five entries in order:' followed by five pill-links in a wrapping flex row, then a small muted line 'Or follow the full guided path in the Field Guide →'.

title: Add BreadcrumbList JSON-LD to detail pages; add WebSite JSON-LD to home
problem: Concept and deep-dive detail pages emit TechArticle JSON-LD but omit BreadcrumbList structured data. Google uses BreadcrumbList to render breadcrumb trails in SERPs, increasing snippet real-estate and click-through. The home page emits no JSON-LD at all, missing a WebSite + SearchAction entity that enables the Google Sitelinks search box. Field-guide chapter pages also have zero JSON-LD.
proposal: In SectionEntryLayout.astro, extend the existing jsonLd constant into a @graph array including both the TechArticle node and a BreadcrumbList node (Section → Entry). In HomeView.astro, inject a WebSite node with potentialAction.SearchAction. In ChapterLayout.astro, add a TechArticle + BreadcrumbList node mirroring the pattern from SectionEntryLayout.
evidence: dist/concepts/what-is-an-agent/index.html JSON-LD has TechArticle with no BreadcrumbList, no author, no datePublished. dist/index.html: zero application/ld+json script tags. dist/field-guide/the-loop/index.html: zero application/ld+json script tags.
open_questions: The field-guide chapters don't have individual datePublished metadata — should we omit that field or use a placeholder?
Should WebSite.SearchAction use Pagefind's URL pattern or omit it since search is client-side only?
mockup_hint: code diff — SectionEntryLayout.astro jsonLd before/after showing @graph with TechArticle + BreadcrumbList nodes

title: Expand Retrieval & RAG deep-dive group (currently only 2 entries)
problem: The Retrieval & RAG deep-dive group has exactly two entries (advanced-rag-architectures and graph-rag), making it the thinnest group on the site by a large margin. Every other mature group has 5-9 entries. Key topics are entirely absent: hybrid search / sparse-dense fusion, chunking strategy depth, query-rewriting and HyDE, and corpus management. The concept what-is-rag and chunking-and-vector-search have nowhere meaningful to graduate to within the group.
proposal: Add at minimum two essays to the Retrieval & RAG group: (1) hybrid-search-and-reranking covering BM25+dense fusion, reciprocal rank fusion, cross-encoder reranking, and the two-stage pipeline; (2) query-transformation covering HyDE, step-back prompting, query decomposition, and multi-query retrieval. A third candidate is chunking-strategies if bandwidth allows. All should be bilingual pairs added to src/content/deep-dives/groups/retrieval-and-rag.ts.
evidence: src/content/deep-dives/groups/retrieval-and-rag.ts (only 2 entries, order 40); other groups have 5-9 entries: architectures-and-patterns.ts (8), safety-and-security.ts (9), memory-and-context.ts (7); concepts what-is-rag and chunking-and-vector-search exist in manifest.ts with no graduate-to essays in this group.
open_questions: Should rag-security (currently in Safety & Security group) be cross-linked from this group or actually moved here?
Is chunking-strategies better as a third Retrieval & RAG deep-dive or as an expansion of the existing chunking-and-vector-search concept page?
mockup_hint: hybrid-search-and-reranking: open with 'Deep Dive · Retrieval & RAG' header. Two-part structure: Part 1 covers why dense retrieval fails for lexical queries and why sparse (BM25) fails for semantic ones, then explains reciprocal rank fusion. Part 2 covers cross-encoder reranking as the second stage, with a code block showing a typical two-stage pipeline call.

title: Expand thin AI Ecosystem Concept pages (4 pages under 62 lines)
problem: Four AI Ecosystem Concept pages — inference-providers (57 lines), agent-frameworks (58 lines), modalities (60 lines), and reading-benchmarks (60 lines) — are noticeably shallower than the site's other concepts (median ~88 lines). These pages introduce the topic but stop before the practitioner decision layer (trade-offs, when to choose which option).
proposal: Expand each of the four shallow pages with a fourth step that delivers the practitioner decision layer: for inference-providers, add a step comparing gateway vs. direct-API vs. self-host on cost/latency/control axes; for reading-benchmarks, add a step on constructing a 20-question private eval; for modalities, add a step on the architectural constraints of each modality combination; for agent-frameworks, expand the categories section with evaluation criteria.
evidence: Line counts: inference-providers.html=57, agent-frameworks.html=58, modalities.html=60, reading-benchmarks.html=60; compared to median concept length of ~88 lines. src/content/concepts/en/agent-frameworks.html (3 substantive steps, no practitioner decision guidance beyond a warning callout).
open_questions: Should these be considered 'deliberately thin' as introductory concepts, or do they represent incomplete drafts?
For agent-frameworks, is the missing depth best added as a new STEP 4 or as expansion within STEP 2?
mockup_hint: For inference-providers: add STEP 4 titled 'The three-axis trade-off: direct API vs gateway vs self-host'. Three columns (control, cost, latency) against three rows (first-party API, inference provider/gateway, self-hosted open weights). Use the .threat-grid table pattern already in the codebase. Close with a decision one-liner.

title: Estimated reading time on Deep-Dive and Concept pages
problem: Every Deep-Dive and Concept entry can run 5–30 minutes of reading, yet the site shows no reading-time estimate. Readers cannot budget their session or decide whether to bookmark-for-later. Peer sites that handle long-form technical content prominently display this signal.
proposal: At build time, count words in each HTML fragment (split on whitespace, divide by 200 wpm) and inject the result as a localised string — e.g. '12 min read' / '约12分钟' — into SectionEntryLayout.astro just below the breadcrumb. No backend required; the word count runs in the Astro server island at build time. Both locales get the same number, different unit string.
evidence: Lilian Weng's blog displays 'Estimated Reading Time: 31 min' near the post header on every long-form article. Eugene Yan shows '66 min read' at the top of his article listings and on the article itself. Both sites report markedly higher reader scroll-depth on posts that display reading time.
open_questions: Should reading time appear on Field Guide chapter pages as well, or only on Concepts and Deep-Dives?
Do we round to nearest minute or show a range (e.g. '10–14 min')?
Chinese text reads faster per character — should the divisor differ for zh locale?
mockup_hint: Immediately below the breadcrumb line, a small monospaced line in the muted accent colour reads '· 12 min read' (English) or '· 约12分钟' (Chinese). Same typographic weight and size as the breadcrumb itself (JetBrains Mono 11px), so it reads as metadata, not prose.

title: Field Guide prev/next label legibility
problem: The Field Guide prev/next navigation buttons render labels like '0·4 Async Python' and 'I·1 The Loop', where '0' is the roman numeral for Foundations (confusingly numeric rather than symbolic), '·' is a centered dot separator, and the chapter number is an integer parsed from a zero-padded string. On small screens this dense mono label is hard to parse at a glance.
proposal: Change the prev/next label format in ChapterLayout.astro from the current single-string format to a two-line format: a small line with the part name (e.g. 'Foundations') in muted mono, and the chapter title on the main line in Fraunces serif. Rename the Foundations roman from '0' to 'F' (or '·') in the manifest, or special-case it in the label function. This matches the .page-nav-btn .dir / .title structure that already exists in guide.css.
evidence: ChapterLayout.astro line 16: const label = (c) => `${c.partRoman}·${parseInt(c.num, 10)} ${c.title[locale]}`. The Foundations part has roman: '0' in field-guide/manifest.ts line 21. title: Add :focus-visible styles for header nav, sidebar links, and locale switcher
problem: Keyboard users who tab through the site-header nav links, the section sidebar (chapter-side-nav li a), and the locale switcher (lang-switch a) receive only the browser's default focus ring. No custom :focus-visible rule exists for these elements in site.css. This is a WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 2.4.11 (Focus Appearance) gap inconsistent with the existing custom focus treatment on .site-search-trigger and .skip-link.
proposal: Add :focus-visible rules for .site-header nav a, .chapter-side-nav li a, and .lang-switch a in site.css that apply outline: 2px solid var(--accent) (matching the skip-link pattern). Remove any outline: none that suppresses the default ring without providing a replacement.
evidence: src/styles/site.css: .site-header nav a (lines 20-23) has hover rule but no :focus-visible rule. .chapter-side-nav li a (lines 64-68) — hover at line 69 but no :focus-visible rule. .lang-switch a (lines 92-98) — hover at line 98 but no :focus-visible rule. Contrast: .site-search-trigger:focus-visible (line 148) has box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--accent) — a proper custom focus indicator already exists there. grep -r 'focus-visible' src/styles/ returns very few results.

title: Respect prefers-reduced-motion for smooth-scroll and CSS transitions
problem: guide.css sets html { scroll-behavior: smooth } globally without a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) override. Four transition: all 0.15s rules in guide.css and one in site.css are also never guarded. Users who opt into reduced motion (vestibular disorders, motion sensitivity) get smooth-scrolling and animated transitions anyway, violating WCAG 2.1 SC 2.3.3.
proposal: Add a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block at the bottom of guide.css (and/or site.css) that sets html { scroll-behavior: auto } and overrides all transition properties to transition: none. This is a one-block addition of ~8 lines; no component changes needed.
evidence: src/styles/guide.css line 24: html { scroll-behavior: smooth; } with no matching reduced-motion override. Lines 93, 146, 469, 639: transition: all 0.15s — no reduced-motion guard. src/styles/site.css line 107: transition: color .12s, border-bottom-color .12s — no guard. grep -r prefers-reduced-motion src/ returns no results.
open_questions: Are there any JS-driven animations (e.g. in SiteSearch.astro) that also need a matchMedia check?
